`Z3.set_param` is only called when `parallel` is true; if any previous initialization enabled parallel, constructing a solver with `parallel: false` won’t disable it (global param can leak across solver instances). Consider setting the param to either "true" or "false" based on the keyword, or centralizing this configuration so it’s applied deterministically once.
```suggestion
      Z3.set_param("parallel.enable", parallel ? "true" : "false")
```

```suggestion
    # @param parallel [Boolean] Use Z3's parallel solving algorithm
```

This changes default solver behavior (parallel solving enabled by default) and introduces a new public keyword (`parallel:`), but there’s no test coverage exercising `parallel: false` or asserting the default behavior. Adding a small unit test around initialization would help prevent regressions and catch global-parameter leakage between tests/solvers.
```suggestion

```

`global_options` is defined as an instance method on the `Udb` module, but the new call sites use `Udb.global_options...` (a module/singleton method). If `Udb` is not `extend self`/`module_function` elsewhere, this will raise `NoMethodError` at runtime. Consider defining it as `def self.global_options` (or explicitly `extend self` / `module_function :global_options` in this file) so the call sites are correct regardless of other module setup.
```suggestion
  def self.global_options
```

`Z3.set_param` changes a process-global Z3 setting, but it’s being executed from every `Z3Solver#initialize` without synchronization. If solvers can be created from multiple threads (or different parts of the app with different option values), this can race and flip the global setting unpredictably. Consider setting this once during program initialization (e.g., in CLI setup right after parsing options) or protect the set/check with a class-level mutex and only apply the change when the desired value differs from the last applied value.

Using `Z3Solver.class_eval { @parallel_enabled ... }` for simple reads/writes makes control flow harder to follow and obscures intent. Prefer a clearer class-level accessor (e.g., `class << self; attr_accessor :parallel_enabled; end`) or direct `instance_variable_get/set` on the class, and centralize the “check + warn + set_param + update cached value” logic into a small helper to avoid duplication between the `true` and `false` branches.
```suggestion
    class << self
      extend T::Sig

      sig { returns(T.nilable(T::Boolean)) }
      attr_accessor :parallel_enabled

      sig { params(enabled: T::Boolean).void }
      def set_parallel(enabled)
        previous = @parallel_enabled

        if previous == false && enabled
          Udb.logger.warn "Z3 parallelization was previously disabled, but is now being enabled"
        elsif previous == true && !enabled
          Udb.logger.warn "Z3 parallelization was previously enabled, but is now being disabled"
        end

        @parallel_enabled = enabled
      end
    end

The option key `:z3parallel` is inconsistent with the rest of the CLI options, which use snake_case (e.g., `:config_dir`) and therefore generate dashed flags like `--config-dir`. Consider renaming this to something like `:z3_parallel` so users get a consistent flag name (e.g., `--[no-]z3-parallel`).

      method_option :z3_parallel, type: :boolean, desc: "Use parallel.enable for Z3", default: true

```

In the RBI, `Udb.global_options` is declared without a Sorbet signature/return type, so it will be treated as `T.untyped` and callers won’t get type checking/autocomplete for `parallel_z3`. Consider adding a `sig` returning `Udb::GlobalOptions` here to preserve typing for this new API.
```suggestion

    sig { returns(::Udb::GlobalOptions) }
```
